memo.verdict: Neutral; park; conviction medium. Getlink (GET-FR) at €18.83 (2026-09-25) is a yield-and-optionality hold on a monopoly asset, not a growth case, and it is not compelling at this price. The 'Modal return' on the record's own path is about 12 percent a year over eighteen months (11.9 percent) and about 10.5 percent a year over three years, against the 20 percent bar: a D. The park is on the return, not on any gate: management B, business quality B, predictability C, trackability A, so the park rule is not triggered. The modal path clears 20 percent a year only below about €16.94 over eighteen months and €14.69 over three years. Re-open on any of: the price at or below €17.00; Q3 2026 shuttle yield at or above 4 percent with truck share still rising; Q4 2026 ElecLink monthly auctions holding H1 2026 realised rates; Virgin's rolling-stock financing secured; a 50 basis point fall in ten-year real yields. Bearish only if monthly truck volumes turn down with ferry fares falling, or if Ofgem's ruling pulls provision cash into 2027. Under the drop-through sensitivity (depreciation €260 million, tax 15 percent, finance €10 million higher) the 'Modal return' Element falls from D to F and the recommendation does not change.
case: The thesis: Getlink is a yield-and-optionality hold on a monopoly asset, not a growth case; a 4.5 percent dividend yield plus high-single-digit earnings growth on a concession to 2086, fairly priced at its own five-year median multiple, pays about 12 percent a year over eighteen months and 10.5 percent over three; the parts that would make it interesting (rail liberalisation from 2030, a lower rate environment) sit beyond the horizon and are not the company's to deliver.

The external change is a mild cyclical tailwind on the edge of the profit pool. The cross-Channel market is flat (-0.2 percent over twelve months); shuttle volumes fell in H1 2026 (cars -2 percent, trucks -1 percent). What moves is the competitors' cost base: the three ferry operators' combined fuel and carbon surcharge about €50 a crossing against Eurotunnel's €32 electricity surcharge; the carbon surcharge alone €10 from €3 in 2024; EU ETS on ferries 70 percent of emissions in 2025 and 100 percent in 2026; the UK ETS from July 2026; seafarer wage laws lifting ferry costs 6 to 12 percent; LeShuttle truck share +90 basis points in May and +160 in June 2026, car share +35 basis points to 60.2 percent. Capacity has not eased: up to 13 vessels on Dover-Calais (Bernstein), P&O lost £95 million in 2023, and the tailwind is fuel-price-driven and reversible. Three headwinds: the Entry/Exit System (passenger rollout from April 2026, about 2 percent of passenger shuttle traffic lost, waits tripled to 20 minutes, €80 million spent on pre-registration zones, the September 2026 EU deadline doubted by management, the truck and coach rollout working since October 2025); UK business rates €6 million in 2026, €14 million in 2027, €24 to 27 million by 2028 after the failed VOA appeal; the UK industrial cycle (vehicle output -7.5 percent in H1 2026 to 385,979 units, exports -5.6 percent, about 70 percent of Fixed Link demand UK-driven; sterling unhedged, a 10 percent fall costing €46 million of EBITDA). Bond yields are a further headwind on the multiple: 50 basis points is worth 7 to 10 percent of value.

The internal change is second-order: the dividend re-set; the 2030 plan of 26 February 2026 (€1 billion EBITDA from pricing, traffic and cost; capex €170 to 220 million a year to 2032; no bridge given); the July 2026 guidance rise of 1.5 percent at the midpoint with consensus already above the range; unbundled fares from March 2025 (premium tier 19 percent, yield +4 percent in H1 2026, +3 percent in FY2025, +6 percent at seasonal peaks, Q2 2026 slowed to +3 percent); the €25 million Performance Plan; eco-driving cutting energy use 14 percent; customs bolt-ons (Bongers €7 million, ASA/BIMS €12 million, 67 percent of Electrofer); a €50 million solar programme (48 GWh, 12 percent self-consumption from 2028). No chief-executive change (Leriche since 1 July 2020, reappointed 2024, Vice-Chairman May 2026), no perimeter change, no balance-sheet action (net debt €3,392 million at end-2025, €850 million of bonds refinanced with €600 million). The screen's rule fails. The anchor holders' stake-building is not an operating force; it acts on the multiple.
counter_case: Against the thesis rating (D), from the bull side: Getlink is a mis-modelled compounder of cash returns. The sell-side models ElecLink 2027 revenue at €313 million when 71 percent of capacity has already fetched €256 million, a full-year run-rate above €350 million; it models Fixed Link EBITDA flat when truck share rose 160 basis points in a single month on ferry cost inflation; it ignores that consensus 2030 EBITDA of €954 million sits below a target management has never missed. On that view EPS compounds at 12 percent a year and a multiple supported by a 9.0 percent cost of equity and two anchor buyers at €17.40 to €17.70 re-rates toward 32x for a 20 percent a year return. Conceded: the guidance record is excellent (three consecutive years at or above the ceiling); the ElecLink 2027 consensus line is probably conservative; the Eiffage floor is real. Held: the ElecLink upside is halved by the 50 percent profit share above a 13 percent IRR and the provision already stands at €580 million; Fixed Link EBITDA was flat in H1 2026 at €294 million with opex up 6 percent and Q2 pricing decelerating to 3 percent; below EBITDA the H1 net profit missed by 5.2 percent on depreciation and tax, pointing the drop-through the wrong way; EPS revisions of +0.7 to +2.0 percent over twelve months show the sell-side has already absorbed the EBITDA beats; twelve percent EPS growth would need Fixed Link volume growth, and the volumes are falling.

Against the foundations rating (B): the risks research's FALSE FRIEND profile (June 2026): transient power-grid spreads and deferred capex mask structural cross-Channel volume decay; the ferries, with up to 13 vessels and a low-cost entrant, absorb the surcharges to defend share; Entry/Exit System friction diverts leisure travellers to airlines; UK business rates and the €580 million profit-share liability turn into cash; sterling is unhedged; the 2086 term makes the equity a duration bet into rising yields. The evidence for it is real: truck volumes 31 percent below the 2018 peak; share losses in 2023 to 2025; Q2 2026 pricing at +3 percent; August 2026 cars -4.9 percent; a 5.2 percent net profit miss; capex of €125 million in 2025 against a €170 to 220 million guide. Conceded: the Fixed Link is not growing in volume; the ElecLink windfall is temporary; the currency and rate exposures are structural; the case is a yield case, not a growth case. Held: the thesis does not need volume growth, only price and contracted tolls, which are delivered; the ferry cost inflation is regulatory and has widened since that research (carbon €3 to €10, €50 combined; truck share +160 basis points in June); the H1 2026 results, post-dating it, beat on revenue, EBITDA and cash; the balance sheet (€1.36 billion of cash, an investment-grade operating company, half the debt due after 2040) absorbs the provision and the rates without threatening the dividend over the horizon. Where it bites is the multiple, and the 'Investment Thesis' rating already sits at D for that.
triggers: - Re-open triggers: the price at or below €17.00; Q3 2026 yield at or above 4 percent with truck share still rising (lifts the yield driver to likely and the return toward the C band); Q4 2026 ElecLink auctions holding H1 2026 rates (lifts the 2027 to 2028 EPS path 3 to 5 percent); Virgin's rolling-stock financing secured (by December 2027, the review's third test; would bring €1.50 to €2.00 a share per entrant into the three-year view); a 50 basis point fall in ten-year real yields.
- Bearish triggers: monthly truck volumes turning down with ferry fares falling; an Ofgem ruling that pulls provision cash into 2027.

- Alarm levels (from the monitoring table): Q3 2026 yield below 4 percent; any Q4 2026 monthly auction more than 20 percent below H1 2026 realised rates; a 50 basis point rise in ten-year real yields; ferry fares falling with surcharges unchanged; a monthly passenger shuttle decline beyond 5 percent after the Entry/Exit System full launch; FY2026 depreciation above €250 million or tax above 12 percent; any monthly truck decline; a change in either anchor holder's AMF declaration; a 10 percent sterling fall; an FY2026 EBITDA outturn inside the €835 to 870 million range rather than above it; a dividend below the policy step; the buy share falling below 40 percent.

- Invalidate levels: two consecutive months of truck-share loss with ferry fares falling (the Fixed Link yield driver and the ferry price war risk); Q4 2026 auctions averaging more than 20 percent below H1 2026 realised rates (ElecLink); monthly truck volumes turning down with ferry fares falling (core volume decay); a 25 percent-plus sterling fall threatening the 1.25x debt-service covenant.
- What would change the record's mind on the drop-through: FY2026 depreciation printing below €240 million and tax below 5 percent (upside); above €250 million or 12 percent (alarm).

- Open questions the inputs could not answer: the live thematics file and the ticker sidecar were not among the inputs, so the thematic cross-reference is recorded as not possible; no track-record or lessons file was among the inputs, so overlap with own historical errors is recorded rather than invented; peer relative-strength data is not among the inputs; the €125 million 2025 capex figure in the risks research is discounted against the FactSet line of €192 million as a sub-total or early estimate.
